story: The other British invasion: how UK lingo conquered the US
text: Hopefully Map Men might help with this. [VIDEO] TLDW; We have multiple different root languages in English city names, and you are only thinking one dimensionally, with the Roman Latin root. Cirencester is a good example, pronounced how you might expect while further north the town names get more germanic, and eventually Scandinavian. The video helps it makes sense.
